hourlyCostRateOverrideCents.title: Hourly cost rate override (cents)
hourlyCostRateOverrideCents.description: Employer cost per hour in cents, set by hand instead of the figure derived from payroll. Leave empty: the normal case. To use the derived value.
hourlyCostRateOverrideCents.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. This is an EMPLOYER COST, not a wage: it is not comparable to EmploymentContract.hourlyWage, which is the employee's gross hourly wage and is never used as a cost rate. Integer cents, never a float, so a rate multiplied by logged hours cannot drift (the ActivityCostAllocationSplitter convention).

hourlyCostRateOverrideReason.title: Hourly cost rate override reason
hourlyCostRateOverrideReason.description: Why the derived cost was replaced. Required whenever you set an override: an override with no reason is indistinguishable from a typo six months later.
hourlyCostRateOverrideReason.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. This number reaches a statutory IV3 submission through Shillinq. Free text: the derivation cannot be told 'this employee is seconded and billed at the partner rate', so the reason is the only place that survives.

hourlyCostRateOverrideBy.title: Hourly cost rate override set by
hourlyCostRateOverrideBy.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. Nextcloud user id. A domain-object reference is deliberately NOT used here: this records the human who made an administrative decision, which is a Nextcloud identity, not an Employee record (ADR-046).

hourlyCostRateOverrideAt.title: Hourly cost rate override set at
hourlyCostRateOverrideAt.description: When the override was last changed. An override set before the last salary change is worth reviewing, not an error.
hourlyCostRateOverrideAt.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. ISO 8601 UTC. Read together with the payroll side to tell a stale override from a current one.

hourlyCostAdditions.title: Hourly cost additions
hourlyCostAdditions.description: Employer costs per hour on top of the wage: overhead, equipment, workplace, tooling. Each entry is named and sourced, so a cost figure can be explained line by line.
hourlyCostAdditions.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. The hourly cost is `wageCost + sum(additions)`; there is exactly ONE rate, never a normal one and an overtime one. Line-by-line explicability is what an audit asks for, and a new cost factor is data rather than a schema migration. Shillinq is expected to calculate the overhead and equipment additions, because it holds the ledger those pools live in.

key.title: Addition key
key.description: A short name for the cost factor, for example 'overhead', 'equipment', 'workplace' or 'overtime'.
key.x-notes: Short stable identifier for the cost factor — e.g. `overhead`, `equipment`, `workplace`, `overtime`.
Not an enum: the set is deliberately open (ADR-081), because a jurisdiction, a sector or an audit will want a fourth.

centsPerHour.title: Fixed amount per hour (cents)
centsPerHour.description: A fixed amount added per hour, in cents: the right shape for a cost that does not scale with pay: rent, a workplace, a laptop, management fees. Use this or a percentage of the wage, never both.
centsPerHour.x-notes: A FIXED amount added per hour, in CENTS — the right shape for a cost that does not scale with the wage: rent, a workplace, a laptop, management fees. Integer so that rate x hours cannot accumulate IEEE-754 drift across a quarter of allocations. Set this OR percentageOfWage, never both.

percentageOfWage.title: Percentage of the wage base
percentageOfWage.description: An amount per hour as a percentage of the wage: the right shape for a cost that does scale with pay, such as an overtime surcharge. It is worked out over the wage only, never over the running total. Use this or a fixed amount, never both.
percentageOfWage.x-notes: A RELATIVE amount, as a percentage of the wage base — the right shape for a cost that genuinely scales with pay, such as an overtime surcharge. Applied to the WAGE BASE ONLY, never to the running total: compounding one addition onto another would make the result depend on the order they happen to be listed in. Set this OR centsPerHour, never both.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the amount came from: entered by an administrator, or calculated from the ledger by another app. A figure someone owns ages differently from one a system derives.
source.x-notes: Where the amount came from: `manual` (an administrator typed it) or an app id such as `shillinq` (calculated from the ledger). Distinguishes a figure someone owns from one a system derives — they age differently and are reviewed differently.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: Why this amount, in words. For an amount you entered, the justification; for a calculated one, what it was worked out from. An unexplained cost cannot be defended in a statutory submission.
basis.x-notes: Why this amount, in words. For a manual addition this is the justification; for a calculated one, what it was computed from (e.g. which overhead pool over which hours). An unexplained cost component in a statutory submission is unauditable.

CostAdditionPolicy.title: Cost Addition Policy
CostAdditionPolicy.description: An employer cost that applies per worked hour on top of the wage: overhead, workplace, equipment, management fees. Scoped to everyone under a given collective labour agreement, to a single contract, or to the whole organisation. The most specific scope wins per cost factor: contract beats CLA beats organisation.
CostAdditionPolicy.x-notes: ADR-081 decision 4. Deliberately NOT part of the CLA corpus: a collective labour agreement does not state what an employer's overhead is, and that corpus holds only figures transcribed from published CLA texts with a source citation. Scoping BY a CLA is a convenient way to select a group of employees ('everyone under the ICK CLA carries EUR 25/h for rent and management'), not a claim that the CLA says so.

key.title: Cost factor
key.description: A short name for the cost factor, for example 'overhead', 'equipment', 'workplace' or 'overtime'.
key.x-notes: Short stable identifier for the cost factor — e.g. `overhead`, `equipment`, `workplace`. Not an enum: the set is deliberately open, so a new cost factor is data rather than a schema migration.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Who this applies to: everyone in the organisation, everyone under a collective agreement, or one contract only. The most specific one wins.
scope.x-notes: Which population this policy applies to. `organisation` — everyone; `cla` — everyone whose contract names claId; `contract` — one contract only. The most specific scope carrying a given key wins, so a contract-level figure overrides the CLA-wide one for that key without disturbing the others.

claId.title: Collective labour agreement
claId.description: Which collective agreement's population this covers. Required when the scope is a collective agreement; ignored otherwise.
claId.x-notes: The CLA (Dutch: CAO) whose population this policy covers. REQUIRED when scope is `cla`, ignored otherwise. Matches EmploymentContract.cao.

contractId.title: Employment contract
contractId.description: Which single contract this covers. Required when the scope is one contract; ignored otherwise.
contractId.x-notes: UUID of the single EmploymentContract this policy covers. REQUIRED when scope is `contract`, ignored otherwise.

centsPerHour.title: Fixed amount per hour (cents)
centsPerHour.description: A fixed amount added per hour, in cents: the right shape for a cost that does not scale with pay: rent, a workplace, a laptop, management fees. Use this or a percentage of the wage, never both.
centsPerHour.x-notes: A FIXED per-hour amount in CENTS. The shape most employer overheads actually have — rent and management fees do not scale with an individual's salary. Set this OR percentageOfWage, never both.

percentageOfWage.title: Percentage of the wage base
percentageOfWage.description: An amount per hour as a percentage of the wage: the right shape for a cost that does scale with pay, such as an overtime surcharge. Use this or a fixed amount, never both.
percentageOfWage.x-notes: A RELATIVE per-hour amount, as a percentage of the wage base. Applied to the wage base only, never compounded onto other additions. Set this OR centsPerHour, never both.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: Why this amount, in words. For an amount you entered, the justification; for a calculated one, what it was worked out from. An unexplained cost cannot be defended in a statutory submission.
basis.x-notes: Why this amount, in words — what it covers and how it was arrived at. REQUIRED. An unexplained cost component reaches a statutory submission via Shillinq and cannot be defended there; 'EUR 25/h overhead' is a number, 'rent and management fees, FY2026 budget over billable hours' is an answer.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the amount came from: entered by an administrator, or calculated from the ledger by another app. A figure someone owns ages differently from one a system derives.
source.x-notes: Where the amount came from: `manual` when an administrator set it, or an app id such as `shillinq` when it was calculated from the ledger. Distinguishes a figure someone owns from one a system derives — they age differently and are reviewed differently.

effectiveFrom.title: Effective from
effectiveFrom.description: First date this applies. Leave empty if it has always applied: costing last year's hours at this year's overhead would quietly restate history.
effectiveFrom.x-notes: First date this policy applies. Null means it has always applied. Overheads are re-budgeted; costing last year's hours at this year's overhead would silently restate history.

effectiveTo.title: Effective until
effectiveTo.description: Last date this applies. Leave empty while it is still in force. Close an old policy here rather than deleting it, so past allocations stay explicable.
effectiveTo.x-notes: Last date this policy applies. Null means currently in force. A superseded policy is closed by setting this rather than deleted, so a historical allocation stays explicable.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: The administration this policy belongs to.

overtimeToeslagPercentages.title: Overtime surcharge percentages (contract override)
overtimeToeslagPercentages.description: Overtime surcharges for this contract, instead of what the collective agreement says. Leave empty: the normal case. To follow the agreement. These are the surcharge, not the total: 50 means 150% of the normal hourly wage. Setting this replaces the agreement's overtime terms in full.
overtimeToeslagPercentages.x-notes: Per-category overwerktoeslag for THIS contract, overriding whatever the CAO says. Null — the normal case — means the CAO's own overtime article applies, resolved through CaoRegistry. Terms are company-wide by default and individual only by exception, so the absence of a value here is the meaningful state, not an unfinished one. Percentages are the SURCHARGE, not the total: 50 means 150% of the normal hourly wage is paid for that hour. When set, the override wins IN FULL rather than merging per category — a partial merge would silently combine two documents' terms and produce a set of rules that exists in neither.

doordeweeks.title: Weekday
doordeweeks.description: Surcharge percentage for overtime on an ordinary weekday.

zaterdag.title: Saturday
zaterdag.description: Surcharge percentage for overtime on a Saturday.

zondag.title: Sunday
zondag.description: Surcharge percentage for overtime on a Sunday.

feestdag.title: Public holiday
feestdag.description: Surcharge percentage for overtime on a public holiday.

overtimeTermsOverrideReason.title: Overtime terms override reason
overtimeTermsOverrideReason.description: Why this contract departs from the collective agreement's overtime terms. Required whenever you set an override: departing from a collective agreement is an individual arrangement someone has to be able to justify, and it feeds a cost figure that reaches a statutory submission.
overtimeTermsOverrideReason.x-notes: Why this contract departs from the CAO's overtime article. REQUIRED whenever overtimeToeslagPercentages is set. Departing from a collective agreement is an individual arrangement someone negotiated and someone must be able to justify — an unexplained override is indistinguishable from a data-entry error, and it feeds a cost figure that reaches a statutory submission.

leaveEntitlementOverrideDays.title: Leave entitlement (contract override)
leaveEntitlementOverrideDays.description: Full-time holiday days for this contract, instead of what the collective agreement says. Leave empty to follow the agreement. Statutory minimums still apply: an override below them is a violation, not an exception.
leaveEntitlementOverrideDays.x-notes: Full-time vakantiedagen for THIS contract, overriding the CAO's leaveEntitlement. Null means the CAO applies. Statutory minimums still bind: nl-verlof-wettelijk-minimum is evaluated against the resulting entitlement, so an override below the wettelijk minimum is a violation rather than a permitted exception.

leaveTermsOverrideReason.title: Leave terms override reason
leaveTermsOverrideReason.description: Why this contract departs from the collective agreement's leave entitlement. Required whenever you set an override.
leaveTermsOverrideReason.x-notes: Why this contract departs from the CAO's leave entitlement. REQUIRED whenever leaveEntitlementOverrideDays is set, for the same reason the overtime override needs one.

TimeEntry.x-notes: hours-process-redesign: this cost-allocation extension moved from Timesheet to TimeEntry — allocation describes what a specific booking was worked on, which is per-entry, not per-period. The former Timesheet-level copies were dropped rather than kept as denormalized aggregates: no PHP, manifest or event-contract consumer reads them (PayrollGLPostService and the approved-time-entry CloudEvent were checked), so a retained copy would be a dead declaration. None of these three properties ever appears on a form: they are written by integrations, not people.

domainObjectRef.title: Domain object reference
domainObjectRef.description: The external case or dossier this booking was worked on, when hours are logged from another application.
domainObjectRef.x-notes: Optional UUID of the external domain object — a dossiq case, a decidiq dossier, anything outside humaniq (ADR-107 decision 6, renumbered from ADR-081). Plain string, not a $ref relation, because the target schema does not exist in humaniq (ADR-062 rule 7 — the same reasoning as projectId and clientRef). Distinct from projectId: a case is not a project, and conflating them would make the resulting cost allocation ambiguous about what it is costing.

domainObjectType.title: Domain object type
domainObjectType.description: Which app and record type the reference points at.
domainObjectType.x-notes: Format `<app>:<schema>` — e.g. `dossiq:case` (ADR-107 decision 6, renumbered from ADR-081). The app id is the `<id>` in that app's appinfo/info.xml, so this literal moves when an app is renamed and NOT before: procest became dossiq and decidesk became decidiq. Nothing writes this field yet, which is the only reason correcting the example is free; once hours are booked the literal is frozen in stored data. Without it a bare UUID is unresolvable: humaniq cannot ask 'which app owns this?' and neither can the receiving bookkeeping app. Set together with domainObjectRef or not at all.

allocationKey.title: Ledger allocation key
allocationKey.description: The bookkeeping category these hours are charged to, filled in by the connected bookkeeping system.
allocationKey.x-notes: The ledger dimension the resulting cost is booked against, OPAQUE to humaniq (ADR-081 decision 5). For a Dutch municipality this is the BBV taakveld code the domain app resolved from its own classification (procest: caseType.iv3Taakveld); another jurisdiction books against something else entirely. humaniq deliberately does not model, validate or translate it — Shillinq owns the taakveld catalogue, and a BBV-shaped field in an HR app would couple humaniq to one country's accounting law. Stamped by the app that logs the hours, at the moment it logs them, so the allocation reflects the classification in force then rather than a later reclassification. Never hand-typed by an employee (product decision 5/6); outside every includeFields allowlist.
